title: Set up a two-radio repeater
summary: Connect two RF-5800V-HH radios and confirm a training call passes through the repeater.
equipment: Two Harris RF-5800V-HH handhelds, matching antennas and batteries, and Harris retransmit cable 12011-0230-A050
requires: Two test stations and approved training channel assignments
A supervised bench or training site with room to lay out the cable
Firmware versions and the approved retransmit settings for both radios
An approved input/output pair: the handout specifies more than 20% frequency separation and no harmonic relationship; do not improvise a pair.

steps.title: Lay out the two radios
steps.detail: With the radios powered off, fit the antennas and battery packs. Label one radio RX and the other TX for the path under test. Connect cable 12011-0230-A050 to the side connector of each radio and fully extend its 50 ft length.
steps.check: Both side connectors are secure and the cable has no tight coils.

steps.title: Set the training channels
steps.detail: Power on each radio and select its approved preset. Match the receiving radio to the input channel and the transmitting radio to the output channel for the path under test.
steps.check: The test stations and repeater agree on which channel is the input and which is the output.

steps.title: Apply the handout’s general settings
steps.detail: On each RF-5800V-HH, press [8-PGM] → CFIG → GENERAL. The handout specifies FM TRANSMIT TONE: ON; SILENCE BEEPS?: NO; ROBUST PREAMBLE: ON; POWER MANAGEMENT: ON; ANC CONNECTOR: ENABLE. Check these against the equipment version before continuing.
steps.check: Both radios match the handout’s general settings and the approved training configuration.

steps.title: Enable retransmit mode
steps.detail: On the RF-5800V-HH, press [3-MODE], select RETRANSMIT and press Enter. The handout specifies ON-SYNC for firmware before 6.0 and ON-ASYNC for 6.0 and later. Confirm the applicable choice against the radio's firmware and approved setup.
steps.check: Each radio displays the intended retransmit mode.

steps.title: Confirm the relayed path
steps.detail: Have one test station transmit a short identified call on the approved input channel. The other station listens on the approved output channel and reports what it received.
steps.check: The listening station hears the complete call on the output channel.

check: Repeat the test and record the mode, which path was tested and whether the receiving station heard the complete call.
avoid: Keep the two repeater radios separated by the full cable length during testing. Closely spaced radios can interfere with each other.

troubleshooting.symptom: Input is heard, but the call is absent on the output
troubleshooting.action: Check both side connectors, the approved retransmit settings and the firmware-specific mode.

troubleshooting.symptom: Reception drops when the other radio transmits
troubleshooting.action: Check cable extension and separation. Ask the instructor to review the channel assignments and antenna placement.

title: Program a fixed-frequency radio channel
summary: Enter and verify an assigned FIX channel on a Harris RF-5800H-MP manpack.
equipment: Harris RF-5800H-MP manpack, suitable antenna or approved test load, and assigned training channel worksheet
requires: Authorization to edit the specified training channel
Approved RX and TX frequencies, modulation and other channel settings

steps.title: Open the channel menu
steps.detail: Press [PGM], then select MODE → PRESET → CHANNEL.
steps.check: The CHANNEL NUMBER screen is open.

steps.title: Select the assigned channel
steps.detail: Enter the worksheet's channel number and press Enter. Confirm it before proceeding. Channel 000 is the manual channel.
steps.check: The displayed channel number matches the assigned preset.

steps.title: Enter the channel settings
steps.detail: Enter the assigned receive and transmit frequencies on their respective screens. Choose the assigned modulation and review the applicable options as they appear. The prompts depend on the selected modulation.
steps.check: The displayed entries match the worksheet before saving.

steps.title: Save and verify
steps.detail: Use Enter to accept the fields and finish the preset. Open the assigned channel again and compare the saved entries against the worksheet. Perform a brief test with a second authorized station when the exercise calls for it.
steps.check: The correct preset retains the expected settings after reopening.

check: Verify the channel number, RX, TX and modulation before the first authorized transmission.
avoid: Use the assigned training worksheet for frequencies, modulation and power settings.

troubleshooting.symptom: The expected menu option is missing
troubleshooting.action: Check the selected modulation and channel. The handout shows additional options for USB and LSB.

troubleshooting.symptom: Settings appear to have been lost
troubleshooting.action: Reopen the assigned preset and confirm that each field was accepted with Enter.

title: Connect a Windows PC to a radio over USB
summary: Set up the RF-7800H-MP direct USB network connection and confirm it responds to ping.
equipment: Harris RF-7800H-MP, Windows training PC, model-compatible USB data cable and approved Harris network radio driver package
requires: Permission to install the driver and edit the training PC network adapter
Approved radio and PC addresses and subnet mask for the isolated link

steps.title: Confirm the radio address
steps.detail: From [8PGM], use CONFIG → NETWORK → INTERFACE to find the Ethernet and ADDRESS settings for DIRECT USB. The handout uses a manually addressed lab connection with the radio DHCP server disabled. Note the radio address and leave the menu with [CLR].
steps.check: You have the exact approved radio address for this link.

steps.title: Locate the radio network adapter
steps.detail: Install the approved Network Radio Driver Installer package if needed. Connect the radio and open Control Panel → Network and Internet → Network and Sharing Center → Change adapter settings. Find the RNDIS connection.
steps.check: The RNDIS adapter appears after the radio is connected.

steps.title: Set IPv4 on the RNDIS adapter
steps.detail: Open the RNDIS adapter properties. Select Internet Protocol Version 4 (TCP/IPv4), open Properties and choose the manual address option. Enter the approved PC address and mask for the radio link.
steps.check: The PC address is different from the radio address and belongs to the same approved subnet.

steps.title: Test the link
steps.detail: Open Command Prompt and run ping against the radio address you recorded. Check the USB connection and both address settings if the radio does not reply.
steps.check: Command Prompt shows replies from the expected radio address.

check: Identify the adapter you changed and record whether ping reached the radio.
avoid: Apply the static address to the radio's RNDIS adapter. Keep the normal Wi-Fi and Ethernet settings as configured.

troubleshooting.symptom: RNDIS does not appear
troubleshooting.action: Confirm the radio is connected, check the USB data cable and verify the approved driver is installed.

troubleshooting.symptom: Ping times out
troubleshooting.action: Check the radio address, the PC address and subnet mask, then reseat the cable and test again.

title: Send a test message over a radio data link
summary: Bring RF-6551H Tactical Chat to Ready and exchange a short training message with another station.
equipment: RF-7800H-MP, Windows PC with RF-6551H Tactical Chat version 2.0 or later, and a connected training station
requires: An instructor-approved shared training plan already loaded on both radios
Antenna connected and radio scanning on the assigned training net
A working PC-to-radio USB network link

steps.title: Record the radio identity
steps.detail: Find the radio's DIRECT USB Ethernet address in the configuration menu. While scanning, press [7OPT], select RADIO, then press Enter to cycle to RADIO NAME. Record the name exactly as displayed.
steps.check: You have both the radio address and name.

steps.title: Confirm the app sees the radio
steps.detail: Open Tactical Chat. If the status shows No Radio Communications, expand Options. Enter the radio IP in the Ethernet address field and its exact radio name in Set Self Address. Close and reopen the application, then check for Ready.
steps.check: The status shows Ready and My Station displays the expected name.

steps.title: Exchange a training message
steps.detail: Select or type the partner station's radio name in Talking To. Confirm the radio is still scanning, then send a short, agreed test message and ask the partner to reply.
steps.check: Both stations receive and can read the expected test message.

check: Confirm two-way delivery. Record the station labels and the time of the test.
avoid: Use only the approved test message and assigned radio identity during the exercise.

troubleshooting.symptom: No Radio Communications persists
troubleshooting.action: Verify ping to the connected radio, compare the address and spelling in Options, then reopen the app.

troubleshooting.symptom: Ready appears, but the partner receives nothing
troubleshooting.action: Check the partner name and ask the instructor to verify the radios are scanning under the same training plan.

title: Plot a radio link in Radio Mobile
summary: Create a point-to-point terrain profile and export it with the assumptions used in the simulation.
equipment: Radio Mobile desktop, SRTM elevation data and two sample endpoints
requires: A practice map area and approved sample coordinates
Endpoint and system inputs for the simulation

steps.title: Extract an elevation map
steps.detail: Open Options → Internet and review the SRTM data settings. Open File → Map properties, choose the training area and size, and click Extract.
steps.check: The displayed terrain covers both practice endpoints.

steps.title: Place two units
steps.detail: Select each site on the map and use Network Properties to place a named unit at the cursor. You can also enter the coordinates. Give each endpoint a distinct name.
steps.check: The two units appear at the intended coordinates.

steps.title: Assign the network and inputs
steps.detail: In Network Properties, use Membership to put both units in the same training network. Review the network and equipment inputs on the Parameters and Systems tabs.
steps.check: Both units are listed in the network with the intended simulation inputs.

steps.title: Open and export the profile
steps.detail: Open the Radio Link tool and assign the transmitter and receiver. Review the terrain between them. Use Edit → Export to save the profile.
steps.check: The profile shows the selected endpoints in the correct order.

check: Save the profile with its endpoint names and assumptions. Use a separate authorized field check to confirm real reception.
avoid: Use training coordinates and keep track of any default equipment settings that could change the prediction.

troubleshooting.symptom: An endpoint is missing from the Radio Link tool
troubleshooting.action: Check that both named units belong to the same network under Membership.

troubleshooting.symptom: Terrain looks flat or incomplete
troubleshooting.action: Check the SRTM data settings and extract a map that covers the whole path.

title: Conduct a two-station radio check
summary: Use a short call and a signal-strength and readability report to verify a voice path.
equipment: Two training radios with appropriate antennas and assigned station identifiers
requires: An approved training channel and permission to transmit
A second operator who can report what they hear

steps.title: Confirm the channel and identifiers
steps.detail: Agree on the assigned channel and station identifiers. Listen before calling and follow the net's permission rules.
steps.check: The channel is available and both operators know their assigned identifiers.

steps.title: Request a radio check
steps.detail: Call the receiving station first, identify your own station, say RADIO CHECK and finish with OVER.
steps.check: The receiving station hears the call and knows a reply is requested.

steps.title: Report strength and readability
steps.detail: The receiving operator reports signal strength first and readability second. For example, 5 by 5 means loud and clear in the handout. If the signal is weak or the speech is hard to read, say which.
steps.check: Both operators can tell whether the issue was strength, readability or both.

steps.title: Confirm the return path
steps.detail: Acknowledge the report. If the exercise requires a check in both directions, ask the other station to initiate the same short check. End with OUT when the exchange is finished.
steps.check: Both directions have a recorded result.

check: Record the result in each direction, including the strength and readability or whether the call received no reply.
avoid: Keep test transmissions brief and wait for permission on a directed net.

troubleshooting.symptom: No reply after the call
troubleshooting.action: Confirm the selected channel and that the other operator is listening. Follow local net procedures before trying again.

troubleshooting.symptom: Signal is strong but words are unclear
troubleshooting.action: Report the readability problem separately and ask for a short repeat.

title: Size a half-wave dipole
summary: Calculate the starting wire length, split it into two equal arms, and understand what still needs tuning.
equipment: Calculator, measuring tape and the wire/installation details for the intended dipole
requires: The assigned frequency in MHz
A known half-wave dipole design; this estimate is not for every antenna type
For construction and testing: suitable supports, feedline, matching arrangement and the equipment’s tuning procedure

steps.title: Confirm the units and design
steps.detail: Write the intended frequency in MHz. Use the handout’s physical half-wave formula, 468 divided by frequency, for an initial total length in feet. This guide sizes the two wire arms; it does not specify a mast or complete installation.
steps.check: The frequency is in MHz and the intended antenna is a half-wave dipole.

steps.title: Calculate the full wire length
steps.detail: For the handout’s 7.5 MHz example, divide 468 by 7.5: the total is 62.4 ft, approximately 19.020 m. Use the calculator above for your assigned frequency.
steps.check: Your result represents both arms together, not one arm.

steps.title: Split the length equally
steps.detail: Divide the total by two. The example gives 31.2 ft per arm, approximately 9.510 m. Label the centre feedpoint and both equal arms on your sketch before measuring the wire.
steps.check: Adding the two arm lengths reproduces the total.

steps.title: Plan the match and verification
steps.detail: Treat the result as a starting estimate. Follow the chosen antenna’s installation and tuning instructions; mounting, nearby objects and the feed arrangement affect the final match. Check tuning before trimming.
steps.check: The estimate is recorded separately from any measured, tuned result.

check: Your worksheet states frequency, total length, each arm’s length and units, with tuning still identified as a separate step.
avoid: Do not use the total length for each arm or apply this formula to a gamma-match design without its dimensions. Keep any erected antenna clear of overhead electrical lines.

troubleshooting.symptom: The answer seems far too long or short
troubleshooting.action: Check the MHz input and whether the result is in feet or metres; metres = feet × 0.3048.

troubleshooting.symptom: The two arms do not add up to the total
troubleshooting.action: Recalculate 468/f for the total and 234/f for each arm; avoid rounding until the last step.

title: Program an RF-5800V voice net
summary: Work through the six net settings, then compare the saved configuration with your assigned net sheet.
equipment: RF-5800V-HH, fitted antenna, charged battery, assigned net sheet and a second station for a radio check
requires: A designated net slot that you are authorized to modify
Assigned RX/TX frequencies, voice settings, squelch, power and net name
The prescribed COMSEC profile already available through local procedures; this guide does not create or distribute keys
This handout describes a fixed-frequency net with Advanced Repeater disabled. Use the separate retransmit guide for repeater operation.

steps.title: Open the assigned net slot
steps.detail: Press [8-PGM] → NORM → NET. Select the net to modify. Set Active in List to Yes, Net Type to Fixed Frequency and Advanced Repeater to No for this procedure.
steps.check: The selected slot is the one on your worksheet; an unrelated net has not been overwritten.

steps.title: Enter receive and transmit frequencies
steps.detail: Open FREQ and enter the assigned RX and TX values separately. Set Receive Only according to the task; the two-way voice example uses No. The example frequency on source page 10 is not a channel assignment.
steps.check: RX, TX and Receive Only match the worksheet exactly.

steps.title: Apply the assigned COMSEC profile
steps.detail: Open COMSEC and select the prescribed existing key reference and crypto mode. The handout’s example labels are not instructions to reuse an example key.
steps.check: Both stations use the required profile. If it is unavailable, resolve that before testing.

steps.title: Match the voice and squelch settings
steps.detail: Under DATA/VOC, set Data/Voice, D/V Type and FM deviation from the net sheet. Under SQUELCH, match the specified digital squelch and analog squelch type. Source pages 12–13 show the fields.
steps.check: The two stations agree on these settings; do not assume frequency alone is enough.

steps.title: Set power and label the net
steps.detail: Under POWER, choose the assigned transmit power. Under NAME, enter the net name. Use CLR to return to the general screen as shown on page 15.
steps.check: The intended net is identifiable and its displayed settings agree with the assigned values.

steps.title: Reopen the settings and make a radio check
steps.detail: Reopen the net and compare each saved field with the worksheet. Select the intended net and coordinate a short identified radio check with the second station.
steps.check: The partner hears the call and you hear the reply. Record the result without recording key material.

check: All six setting groups match the assigned sheet and the two-way radio check succeeds.
avoid: The handout’s frequencies, net name, key label and mode are examples, not universal defaults. Do not copy them into an operational net.

troubleshooting.symptom: The partner cannot hear the call
troubleshooting.action: Check selected net, TX/RX agreement and Receive Only before changing power.

troubleshooting.symptom: A signal is present but speech is absent or unreadable
troubleshooting.action: Compare voice type, deviation, squelch and the prescribed COMSEC profile at both stations.

troubleshooting.symptom: The wrong net name appears
troubleshooting.action: Return to NET and verify which slot was edited before making further changes.

title: Configure an RF-5800V scan list
summary: Choose which nets to monitor, set the priority nets, and check the scan timing against your task.
equipment: RF-5800V-HH with existing programmed nets and a coordinated test station
requires: An approved list of existing nets to monitor
Assigned priority transmit/receive nets and timing values
Radio firmware/menu labels checked against the operator manual; this handout covers configuration, not the scan activation control

steps.title: Build the scan list
steps.detail: Press [8-PGM] → SCAN → LIST → ADD. Add each assigned existing net and confirm with Enter. The source uses Net 01 only as an example.
steps.check: Every intended net is included and unrelated nets are absent.

steps.title: Set the priority transmit net
steps.detail: Open PRIORITY and set Priority TX to the assigned net. Do not assume the currently heard net is the transmit destination.
steps.check: The priority TX entry agrees with the communication task.

steps.title: Set priority receive monitoring
steps.detail: In PRIORITY, set Enable Priority RX and Priority RX Net as assigned. The source example enables priority reception on Net 02.
steps.check: Priority reception is enabled only when required, with the correct net selected.

steps.title: Configure the timing
steps.detail: Open CONFIG. Set Hang Time, enable Hold Time if required, and set its duration. The slide illustrates 3 seconds and 9 seconds; use your assigned values. It repeats the label “Enable Hold Time” for the duration line, so verify the actual field label on your radio.
steps.check: The enable choice and duration are checked separately; the example timings have not been treated as defaults.

steps.title: Review the configuration and test monitoring
steps.detail: Reopen LIST, PRIORITY and CONFIG to confirm the saved entries. Use the applicable operator-manual control to activate scanning; that control is not shown in this excerpt. With a partner, make identified test calls on the listed nets and confirm reception.
steps.check: Record which test nets were heard and whether priority reception behaved as intended.

check: The scan list, priority entries and timing match the task, and the coordinated monitoring test is recorded.
avoid: Adding a net to the list is not proof that scanning has been activated. The supplied three procedure slides do not identify the activation control.

troubleshooting.symptom: An expected net is not heard
troubleshooting.action: Check that the net exists, is in LIST, and scanning is active using the applicable operator manual.

troubleshooting.symptom: Priority traffic is missed
troubleshooting.action: Check Enable Priority RX and Priority RX Net before changing unrelated settings.

troubleshooting.symptom: The radio appears to linger after traffic
troubleshooting.action: Review Hang Time and Hold Time against the assigned values; use the operator manual for their exact firmware-specific behavior.

title: Check a repeater channel pair
summary: Trace who transmits and who receives before checking the offset, access tone and a relayed call.
equipment: A conventional repeater channel assignment, a compatible subscriber radio and a partner station
requires: Assigned repeater input and output frequencies, stated in the same units
Assigned access tone and subscriber-radio programming instructions
An authorized test window; this is a settings check, not a hardware installation or duplexer-tuning procedure

steps.title: Identify the repeater’s two directions
steps.detail: Write the repeater input as “repeater receives” and output as “repeater transmits.” Keep these labels visible while preparing the subscriber settings.
steps.check: Input/output labels are from the repeater’s point of view.

steps.title: Map the subscriber frequencies
steps.detail: Set the subscriber TX to the repeater input and subscriber RX to the repeater output, using the radio’s own programming instructions. A second subscriber using the same repeater normally uses that same pair.
steps.check: Subscriber TX → repeater RX; repeater TX → subscriber RX.

steps.title: Check the offset direction
steps.detail: If the radio asks for an offset instead of separate TX/RX entries, calculate subscriber TX minus subscriber RX in matching units. A negative result means subscriber TX is below RX. Verify how that particular radio represents the sign before saving.
steps.check: The resulting TX frequency equals the assigned repeater input. Do not choose an offset from a generic band table.

steps.title: Check the access tone
steps.detail: Compare the assigned transmit CTCSS/PL tone with the repeater’s access requirement. Use any receive-tone setting only as specified by the channel plan.
steps.check: The tone value and the direction in which it applies are both checked.

steps.title: Make a brief identified call
steps.detail: Coordinate with the partner, listen first, then make a short identified test call. Confirm that the partner receives it through the repeater and that you receive the reply. Leave a pause between transmissions.
steps.check: Both directions pass a readable call; record the result rather than repeatedly keying the repeater.

check: The subscriber frequencies map to the repeater’s opposite directions, the assigned tone is correct, and a two-way relayed call succeeds.
avoid: Do not tune up on the repeater frequency or key it without an identified call. The source’s band-offset table is illustrative, not authority to select frequencies.

troubleshooting.symptom: You hear the repeater but cannot access it
troubleshooting.action: Check subscriber TX against repeater input and verify the assigned transmit access tone.

troubleshooting.symptom: The partner hears you but you hear no reply
troubleshooting.action: Check subscriber RX against repeater output and verify any required receive-tone setting.

troubleshooting.symptom: Both radios talk directly but not through the repeater
troubleshooting.action: Confirm the pair is not accidentally programmed as simplex. Then verify repeater availability and coverage.

title: Transfer a CPA plan to an RF-7800V
summary: Review the selected station and transfer an approved plan using CPA’s Ethernet/RNDIS option.
equipment: RF-7800V-HH, compatible CPA installation and the radio interface configured according to its operator manual
requires: An approved saved plan and a designated radio that may be reprogrammed
Radio and CPA versions checked for compatibility; this guide follows the supplied RF-7800V CPA application manual
The radio already connected as an RNDIS device, with a reachable assigned IP address
A recovery copy of the existing plan and authorized credentials if the equipment requests them

steps.title: Review the plan before transfer
steps.detail: Confirm the intended station, nets and radio identity in the saved plan. Programming changes the radio configuration; resolve any mismatch before proceeding.
steps.check: You are authorized to replace the configuration on this specific radio.

steps.title: Open Program Radio
steps.detail: In Network View or Topology View, select the intended radio. Choose Actions → Program Radio, or choose Program from its context menu.
steps.check: The left side of the dialog contains only the intended station or stations.

steps.title: Check the connection and destination
steps.detail: Choose Ethernet in Programming Parameters. This manual describes a radio connected as an RNDIS device. Enter that radio’s assigned IP address. Use ipconfig on the PC to inspect its interface; configure the radio interface using its operator manual.
steps.check: The destination is the connected radio, not the PC address or an example address from a handout.

steps.title: Review what will be loaded
steps.detail: Review Programming Options. The manual lists Radio Plan, Keys, Training File and CAM; availability depends on the plan. Inspect the applicable options before starting. Do not include unapproved material in the transfer.
steps.check: The plan and every applicable payload are intended for this radio.

steps.title: Start and verify the transfer
steps.detail: Select Start Programming. Follow the installed version’s status prompts and wait for completion. If it fails, record the error and check connection and addressing before trying again. After success, inspect the intended net and coordinate a radio check.
steps.check: CPA reports completion and the radio’s intended settings and test call are verified.

check: The correct station plan is transferred successfully and the radio configuration and coordinated call are verified.
avoid: The Ethernet option is not proof that an arbitrary physical Ethernet connection is supported. This source requires a configured RNDIS connection. Never reuse example passwords or IP addresses.

troubleshooting.symptom: The radio is unreachable
troubleshooting.action: Check the RNDIS interface, assigned addressing and the radio interface instructions. Do not change unrelated network adapters.

troubleshooting.symptom: Unexpected stations appear in the dialog
troubleshooting.action: Cancel and correct the selection in Network View or Topology View.

troubleshooting.symptom: Programming succeeds but the radio check fails
troubleshooting.action: Compare the selected net and assigned settings with the approved plan; successful transfer alone does not prove a working radio link.
